messages:
Cora_AE: Hey team — quick help. Running a POC for AcmeCorp, their integration is failing with 403 `invalid_organization`.
Cora_AE: They say token is valid on their side. POC env: staging, model=text-gen-2, region=us-west1. Need root cause before tomorrow demo.
Sam_Sales: Noted. Customer sent a curl, attaching below — they masked the key.
Sam_Sales: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX' -H 'X-Redwood-Org: acme' -d '{"input":"hi"}'``` 
Anya_Support: Can you paste the full response body and the request-id from the headers? That helps look up logs.
Cora_AE: Response: `403 {"error":"org_mismatch","expected_org":"acme-prod"}`. No request-id in body, only headers: `x-rw-request-id: rw-5f8c`.
Ben_Platform: Likely the API key is bound to a different org alias. Keys can be bound to org IDs or project scopes — if key was created in acme-prod but they're sending X-Redwood-Org: acme, we'll reject.
Ben_Platform: I can check our key metadata. @Anya_Support can you DM me the last 4 chars of the key or the request-id? I'll query internal key service.
Anya_Support: Sent DM with last4 and request-id.
Infra_Oncall: Checked rbacs: key sk-**** has org_id=org_9072 (display: acme-prod) and scopes=[generate:*,embeddings:read]. The header X-Redwood-Org: acme maps to org_9010 (a different tenant). That's the mismatch.
Infra_Oncall: Short-term fix: have client remove the X-Redwood-Org header so the key's org binding is used, or issue a project-scoped key for the acme alias.
Cora_AE: Got it — customer uses an alias. Can we accept alias mapping? They don't want to rotate keys during the demo.
Ben_Platform: We can support alias mapping but it's controlled by identity provisioning — security needs explicit mapping. For POC, recommended: 1) create a project-scoped API key (bind to their project/org alias), or 2) call with the numeric org_id header `X-Redwood-Org-Id: org_9072`.
Security_Eng: Quick note — allowing alias-to-org auto-mapping can be a security risk if org aliases aren't verified. For enterprise customers we normally require SSO-derived claims or admin consent before mapping.
Cora_AE: Customer asks if we can add a temporary scope instead of a new key (they want minimal friction).
Infra_Oncall: Scopes won't change org binding. If key is created under acme-prod, scopes only control allowed actions, not which org it belongs to.
Anya_Support: I sent the two options to the customer and included a short runbook: 1) remove X-Redwood-Org header, 2) create project-scoped key via console -> Settings -> API Keys, 3) if blocked, use `X-Redwood-Org-Id` with numeric id.
Sam_Sales: Pricing question from main contact: if we have to issue a new project key and they move to dedicated later, will this affect billing or require new contracts?
Cora_AE: For POC keys nothing changes billing. Dedicated capacity discussion can be deferred till POC success. I'll follow up with pricing docs.
DeployBot: key-rotate-trigger: no rotation events for sk-**** in last 90d :eyes:
Security_Eng: If they want alias mapping, we can offer a short-term admin consent flow (manual) but needs sign-off. Recommend not in-demo.
Infra_Oncall: Action items: 1) Anya send runbook to customer (done), 2) Ben check if we can expose numeric org_id in console for easier copy (tracking ticket), 3) Cora confirm with customer which route they pick.
Cora_AE: Thanks everyone — I'll push the runbook and ask customer to try removing header first. Will update thread after they test. :thumbsup:
Sam_Sales: Thanks team, appreciate the quick swarm.
